title: Region-aware compliance export ledger and scheduled delivery orchestration
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Provide tenants with a verifiable, region-aware export mechanism that bundles compliance evidence (PDF/CSV), a signed export ledger (manifest), and optional residency attestations. Scheduled delivery must support recurring time windows, retry/backoff semantics, tenant-specific routing (region or on-prem endpoint), and an audit trail surfaced in the Console dashboard.
proposal: Build a pipeline that produces per-tenant export bundles containing: (1) evidence artifacts (PDF/CSV) generated from the Compliance Evidence Store, (2) a machine-readable export ledger (JSON manifest) that lists file checksums, residency tags, and signing metadata, and (3) an optional signed attestation for customers with residency requirements. Expose scheduling controls in the Console (cron-like UI with timezone awareness and delivery windows), implement delivery channels (S3/GCS buckets, secure FTP, signed HTTPS callback), and add an Export History dashboard with delivery status, size, latency, and failure reasons.
acceptance_criteria: Admin can create a scheduled export for a tenant with: cadence, timezone, target delivery channel, residency filter, and retention snapshot
Export bundles include evidence files (PDF or CSV), a ledger manifest with file-level checksums, and a bundle-level signature verifiable by tenant
Scheduler honors delivery windows and retries with exponential backoff; failures surface as actionable errors in Console and via webhook/email alerts
Console shows Export History with per-bundle metadata: tenant, region tag, bundle size, object counts, delivery duration, attempts, and final status
Delivery routing respects tenant residency: for region-restricted tenants, bundles are only delivered to endpoints within allowed regions or to customer-managed on-prem endpoints
Audit logs record who created/modified the schedule, what files were included, and the final delivery endpoint and checksum results
E2E tests exercise generation, signing, delivery, verification of checksums, and dashboard display for a sample tenant
tasks: Spec: define manifest schema, signing format, and residency tagset (PM+ENG)
Scheduler UX: timezone picker, delivery window, retry policy presets (PM+Design)
Backend: export generator service that pulls evidence, packages files, computes checksums, creates ledger, signs bundle (ENG)
Delivery adapters: S3/GCS, secure FTP, signed HTTPS callback; include region gating (ENG)
Console: Export History view, per-bundle details page, and alerting integration (DES+ENG)
Security review and threat model validation for delivery channels and signing keys (SEC)
E2E test harness and sample tenant demo script (QA+ENG)
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (internal beta): enable for 3 pilot tenants with simple S3 delivery, gather telemetry and failure modes
Phase 2 (select customers): add signed manifests and residency gating, onboard security-reviewed tenants
Phase 3 (general availability): enable all delivery adapters, Console UX polished, public docs and runbook
risks: Incorrect residency enforcement could lead to data exfiltration — mitigated by pre-delivery residency checks and gating in delivery adapters
Signing key management and rotation complexity — mitigate with KMS integration and key-rotation playbook
Large bundles may time out or exceed delivery quotas — mitigate via chunked uploads and streaming packaging
stakeholders: Engineering: Liam Chen (owner), Priya Rao (scheduler), Mateo Alvarez (delivery)
notes: We should aim for a manifest format that is both machine-verifiable and friendly for auditors. Consider including an optional human-readable summary PDF alongside the machine ledger. For tenants that require HSM-backed signing, expose a configuration that routes signing operations to the tenant's KMS. Keep initial UX minimal but extensible.
